name: Gerald Fauth

summary.text: Gerald Fauth is a member of the National Mediation Board, appointed by President Trump in 2017, and the brother-in-law of Senator Richard Burr. SEC court filings made public in October 2021 showed that Burr called Fauth on February 13, 2020, shortly after Burr sold more than $1.6 million in stock, and that Fauth began selling shares within minutes; the SEC said it was investigating both men's trades and sought to enforce a subpoena against Fauth.

sources.title: Burr's Brother-In-Law Called Stock Broker, One Minute After Getting Off Phone With Senator

facts.claim: According to SEC filings, Senator Richard Burr called Fauth on February 13, 2020, shortly after selling more than $1.6 million in stock; the call lasted about 50 seconds, and Fauth then began the process of selling his own shares.
facts.quote: It was previously unknown that Burr and Fauth spoke that day, and that their contact came just before Fauth began the process of dumping stock himself.

sources.title: Burr's Brother-In-Law Called Stock Broker, One Minute After Getting Off Phone With Senator

facts.claim: Fauth sold between $97,000 and $280,000 worth of shares in six companies, several of which fell sharply in the subsequent market downturn.
facts.quote: Fauth sold between $97,000 and $280,000 worth of shares in six companies, several of which were hit hard in the downturn.

facts.claim: In 2021 the SEC asked a court to force Fauth to comply with a subpoena he had not complied with for more than a year; Fauth cited a medical condition. The SEC said it had an ongoing insider-trading investigation into both Burr's and Fauth's trades.
facts.quote: The SEC also revealed that there is an ongoing insider trading investigation into both Burr and Fauth's trades.
